findings.closure_criteria: Saved project, external canonical source and observed results refer to the same method revision, survive reopen, and clearly distinguish browser draft status from independently verified host compatibility. Automate reconciliation only if this real loop exposes material recurring friction.

findings.claim: The authored behavior map and semantic-loss text do not demonstrate that each source behavior has a safe destination/drop/blocker or survives retrieval, memory and platform changes.
findings.consequence: A plausible conversion can omit source escalation, retrieval ranking or memory assumptions and still appear structurally reviewed.
findings.smallest_next_test/task: Populate a per-behavior map for one real source with explicit destination/drop/blocker, evidence class and loss impact; execute one semantic preservation case, one platform-loss case and one boundary case against source and converted skill. Report unsupported/partial behavior rather than parity.

findings.claim: Generated SKILL.md embeds authored instructions as executable skill guidance; source control language must be reviewed and rewritten before use in a host.
findings.consequence: Copying source prompt-chain instructions or hostile knowledge content into the procedure can transform historical data into host authority and carry unintended irreversible behavior.
findings.smallest_next_test/task: Before installation, review the actual skill's authority chain, input-data delimiters, escalation and cancellation; use a source fixture containing conflicting instructions and require the converted host run to treat it as data and stop at its authorized boundary. This is a conversion acceptance case, not a claimed browser injection defect.

findings.claim: Tool permission and unavailable-tool guidance exists as a packaging requirement, but no implemented adapter demonstrates least permission or failure containment.
findings.consequence: A host adapter may demand broader credentials than its method needs, retry unsafe writes, or fabricate successful completion when auth, tool access or dependencies fail.
findings.smallest_next_test/task: Write one adapter tool contract naming auth method, minimum scopes, read/write effects and explicit confirmation/cancellation boundaries; test absent tool and denied auth before any side-effect case, then verify one permitted operation and clean removal with public-safe logs.

findings.claim: Skillz/source pointers supply no fetched runtime knowledge or dependency resolution; a real conversion depending on references needs explicit retrieval/preservation and missing-source behavior.
findings.consequence: A skill can preserve an attractive reference link yet lose the knowledge the source GPT depended on, or quietly rely on changed/unlicensed external content.
findings.smallest_next_test/task: For one necessary reference, pin identity/revision, review reuse rights and choose an allowed snapshot or explicit host retrieval contract; execute a normal reference-dependent case and an unavailable/stale-source case, preserving attribution and reporting the gap instead of inventing missing content. Do not require catalog search to close this test.

initial_reviews.summary: The planner promises source and plans honestly. Actual conversion requires byte-level source provenance, per-behavior loss evidence, reviewed runtime instructions, constrained adapter behavior and explicit reference-dependency handling. None is newly demonstrated by this analytical pass.

Question: Which FoundRy requirements remain incomplete or lack decisive evidence, and what bounded next-series tasks should close them?

Criteria: correct source/history and claims; usable create/recover/edit/target/reference/evidence/export loop; safe private-source and publication boundaries; portable backups and honest host-support claims; task list traced to requirements with measurable closure, without reopening completed scoped work.

Sources: docs/foundry-implementation-plan.md (acceptance contract, no separately named current PRD); docs/portable-skill-foundry.md (September27 product direction); docs/capability-workbench-maturation.md (dated proposals); docs/handoffs/2026-09-20-portfolio-maintenance-codex.md; docs/handoffs/coop-pertition-2026-09-07/README.md and remaining-closeout-2026-09-09.md (F01-F20 completed prototypes, no implicit product adoption); docs/handoffs/2026-10-04-production-reconciliation.md; current source and tests. source-hashes.json records frozen local checkout bytes; Git commit is cross-platform identity.

follow_up.current_state: Capability imports validate and confirm replacement, while the prototype merge planner is separate. A pending confirmation can span intervening local edits or another tab.

follow_up.closure: The user sees the real overwrite scope, can cancel, and cannot unknowingly replace intervening work. Both prior and imported states remain recoverable if conflict occurs.

follow_up.title: Adopt conflict-aware merge import only if justified
follow_up.current_state: The current import contract is confirmed whole-workspace replacement. coop-import-plan does not establish a merge feature in production.
follow_up.action: If real transfer use requires merging, define identity-collision choices, capacity limits and explicit preview/cancel/commit behavior. Integrate the planner without silently changing the replacement contract.
follow_up.closure: Conflicting IDs, renamed projects and capacity overflow yield deterministic reviewable plans. Commit is atomic, cancellations leave state untouched and backups retain original data.

follow_up.title: Keep a precise backup evolution and migration contract
follow_up.current_state: The old migration-design document lists the earlier v1 fields, while the portable foundation adds defaults under the supported envelope. Future incompatible schemas have not been implemented.
follow_up.action: Record current fields/defaulting and compatibility behavior in a dated addendum. Before introducing an incompatible format, define adapter dispatch, exact source retention, dry-run and rollback.
follow_up.closure: Historical backups preserve all supplied fields; unknown schemas fail without writes. Simulated write/readback failure retains recoverable originals. Do not build speculative adapters before a real format requires them.

follow_up.title: Prove backup transfer across real origins
follow_up.current_state: Pages, Replit and local development have separate browser stores. Existing suite roundtrips do not establish a real cross-origin receipt.
follow_up.action: Transfer a disposable public-safe capability backup from Pages to a clean Replit/local context, then back. Include old-format fields and new portability fields; preserve unrelated legacy GPT projects.
follow_up.closure: Field-level/hash comparisons match allowed originals, recovery is inspectable and the separate cgpt-workspace is unchanged. Document origin separation and how to recover without account sync.

follow_up.title: Run bounded non-Chromium acceptance
follow_up.current_state: The current browser evidence is Chromium. It does not establish Firefox/WebKit/Safari compatibility for storage, file import/download or the new conversion stage.
follow_up.action: Choose one meaningful create-to-export/recovery journey in each intended supported browser, starting with the audience's next required browser. Record exact browser/device and source revision.
follow_up.closure: Persistence, imports, Unicode export/download, navigation and recovery behave as specified; failures are reproduced and fixed. Do not claim all-browser support from one run.

follow_up.title: Complete real assistive-technology acceptance for FoundRy
follow_up.current_state: Keyboard/mobile automated cases exist, but no comprehensive FoundRy screen-reader or real zoom acceptance is supplied.
follow_up.action: Define a bounded FoundRy journey with real assistive technology, keyboard navigation, focus recovery, announcements and 200%/400% zoom. Keep unrelated website acceptance under its owner.
follow_up.closure: An actual tester records interaction, focus and announcements for import errors, replacement prompts, stage changes, selected files and clipboard failure. Repair reproduced failures; trees alone do not certify spoken behavior.

follow_up.title: Adopt structured contracts only after outcome need
follow_up.current_state: Inputs, outputs, components and acceptance are authored text. The structured contract parser is a completed experimental API.
follow_up.action: Choose a concrete constraint the exemplar needs to validate, preserve free-text compatibility and define structured fields that serve that constraint. Integrate UI/storage/export only within that scope.
follow_up.closure: Older projects roundtrip, invalid structured inputs produce actionable errors and the intended outcome uses the constraints. Structure alone never becomes behavioral validation.

follow_up.title: Add canonical Skillz selection if real usage warrants it
follow_up.current_state: Skillz is linked and user references are recorded. Search, dependency resolution and installation remain maturation proposals.
follow_up.action: Measure selection/pinning friction from the exemplar. If justified, read the canonical catalog with a pinned source and bounded stale/unavailable handling, preserving attribution.
follow_up.closure: Exports can be reproduced from the selected revision; removal or change of a catalog entry preserves the recorded reference. FoundRy does not become a second catalog source of truth.

follow_up.title: Trial a bounded external-agent handoff
follow_up.current_state: The agent-handoff generator is standalone; FoundRy does not execute arbitrary agents or systems.
follow_up.action: Start with a user-run handoff from the chosen package. Name one task owner, file scope, canonical revision, action/cost limits and evidence-return contract. Only consider an execution adapter after a useful manual trial.
follow_up.closure: One task is implemented and checked reproducibly, with cancellation, inspectable changes, recovery and recorded costs. No credentials or generic backend are required merely to trial the handoff.

follow_up.title: Demonstrate a real prompt outcome
follow_up.current_state: The action-extraction prompt example has expected cases, not a recorded named-model execution outcome.
follow_up.action: Use a public-safe real source document and a fixed rubric to evaluate action items, owners, evidence references, unsupported assumptions and boundary handling in a named environment.
follow_up.closure: Observed output and deviations are retained with model/date/source/package revision. The result is distinguished from its authored expectation and does not imply universal model reliability.

follow_up.title: Demonstrate a real Agent Skill outcome
follow_up.current_state: The existing handoff skill is a packaging example with a manual evaluation recipe; no install/run receipt establishes its host utility.
follow_up.action: Run trigger/non-trigger and repository-handoff cases on a named actual host using its supported skill discovery layout, with public-safe source.
follow_up.closure: The host discovers the skill, produces the required handoff and respects scope on a non-trigger. Versioned evidence explains assistance and failure; installation is separate from performance.

follow_up.title: Demonstrate a real controlled workflow
follow_up.current_state: The release-evidence walkthrough is explicitly synthetic. It does not prove a scheduler or real release process outcome.
follow_up.action: Execute one useful human-controlled workflow with actual receipts, including a failing gate and recovery. Name the owner of each action and retain explicit approvals where required.
follow_up.closure: Observed steps and outputs demonstrate the workflow's intended result and stop correctly on failure. A human-run workflow is labeled as such; no execution engine is inferred.

follow_up.title: Demonstrate the software starter's useful bounded behavior
follow_up.current_state: The generated software inspector parses JSON and reports top-level types; it does not implement arbitrary authored business rules.
follow_up.action: Choose that exact inspector outcome or implement one separately specified missing requirement. Run documented local/browser commands with valid, malformed and hostile text cases.
follow_up.closure: A real intended user can use the tool and its result matches the chosen acceptance. VM smoke checks remain scoped evidence, while business logic and browser usability have their own observations.

follow_up.title: Restore Replit connector and push authentication
follow_up.current_state: Source parity and the preview are verified. The external Replit connector session is expired, and Replit's topic-branch push credentials were rejected.
follow_up.action: Have the owner complete the visible existing-account authentication flow, then verify connector read access and the separate Source Control connection. Preserve current scopes; do not bypass passkeys or repeatedly reconcile clean Git history.
follow_up.closure: A bounded connector read succeeds and Source Control reports the intended GitHub account. A sanctioned topic-branch write can be verified when needed; clean 0/0 is not used as an auth receipt.

follow_up.title: Keep release receipts distinct from dated pending reports
follow_up.current_state: The original maturation and maintenance reports deliberately preserve old pending deployment statements. The new October handoff also separates validation from post-merge delivery.
follow_up.action: Append dated exact-SHA receipts and a clear index to current evidence without rewriting historical conclusions. Use deployment, local, Replit, connector and Notion status separately.
follow_up.closure: A reader can find the current deployed revision and tests without treating an old pending paragraph as current. Future source changes invalidate only affected receipts.

follow_up.title: Review open dependency updates separately
follow_up.current_state: Five open Dependabot PRs propose package updates, including major marked, react-day-picker and Vite-plugin changes. They are proposals rather than made improvements omitted from this release.
follow_up.action: Review PRs 42 and 48â€“51 against current compatibility and advisories. Integrate only tested useful changes through the existing protections; retain minimum-age and lockfile policy.
follow_up.closure: Each accepted update has migration notes and meaningful build/browser/governance evidence; rejected or deferred changes have a reason. No blanket latest-version upgrade is treated as completion.

follow_up.title: Rerun the real protected evaluation at the current package hash
follow_up.current_state: The release checklist explicitly leaves current protected evaluation unchecked because the historical package hash differs. Synthetic regressions test the evaluator, not capability performance.
follow_up.action: Name the maintainer fixture custodian and separate evaluation owner; freeze candidate hash and rubric. Use a genuinely optimizer/developer-unseen external fixture and record exposure history. Keep fixture contents private, execute the approved runtime and return only public-safe result receipts.
follow_up.closure: The result records candidate/runtime hashes, evaluator, custody/exposure status, rubric and pass/fail without leaking fixture content. Used/disclosed cases are consumed; historical evidence does not become current protected approval.

follow_up.title: Verify the manual review-package workflow operationally
follow_up.current_state: The main-only secret materialization, leakage scan, archive and cleanup workflow is committed. No real secret-backed workflow receipt was executed in this release.
follow_up.action: Once the maintainer fixture is available, run the workflow from main, verify failure behavior and cleanup, then inspect the actual uploaded archive against its source inventory.
follow_up.closure: The archive contains only allowed skill files, the temporary fixture is removed on success/failure and protected content is absent. Packaging success is not runtime evaluation or public release approval.
follow_up.conditional_dependencies: Requires maintainer fixture availability/custody and frozen candidate; leak-scan packaging is independent of FND-38 behavioral evaluation.

follow_up.title: Obtain a current ReFolDec release decision and publication receipt
follow_up.current_state: The checklist still defers equilibrium approval and separately authorized deployment. FoundRy being public does not substitute for these capability gates.
follow_up.action: After current protected evaluation and source/license/privacy checks, update the capability decision record and confirm its approved publication surface. Publish only within that explicit scope and verify the served artifact.
follow_up.closure: The exact candidate has an owner-approved decision, approved destination and independent published-byte/version receipt. No public performance or graduation claim precedes the gates.

follow_up.title: Evaluate additional hosts individually
follow_up.current_state: Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenClaw and Perplexity are potential targets, with support explicitly unverified. Success on one does not establish all.
follow_up.action: Select the next host only after the first exemplar/adapter works. Verify its current official package format, method/tool support and manual fallback, then rerun relevant outcome and removal cases.
follow_up.closure: The matrix lists verified, partial, unsupported and untested hosts with dated receipts. Shared source portability does not imply equivalent runtime behavior.

follow_up.title: Adopt demonstrated sibling improvements through review
follow_up.current_state: This release intentionally changes FoundRy only. Separate sibling application ownership and the OverKill universal-governance authority remain in force.
follow_up.action: When a shared need is demonstrated, prepare a compact pinned-source handoff with explicit file scope and validation for the receiving owner; reconcile universal rules upstream.
follow_up.closure: The receiving host acknowledges the handoff and its own tests pass. Source parity is verified per repository; no private sibling material is imported and no silent rule fork is created.

follow_up.title: Make unsaved-memory recovery immediately actionable
follow_up.current_state: Storage denial retains edits and backup works, but the immediate warning lacks an adjacent recovery action and live-announcement semantics.
follow_up.action: Display a persistent accessible unsaved message with a download-newest-backup action and the consequence of refresh/closure. Announce state changes without repeated typing spam.
follow_up.closure: Quota/write denial exposes a backup with the latest edits; status clears only after persistence succeeds. Assistive-technology observation confirms the change is discoverable.

follow_up.title: Expose exact raw malformed-source recovery separately
follow_up.current_state: Malformed bytes are retained in recovery storage, while ordinary workspace backup exports the temporary valid workspace. A visible exact raw-source retrieval path is not established.
follow_up.action: Provide a distinct raw recovery export labeled unparsed/unvalidated, separate from the current workspace backup. Keep raw material as data and preserve it across an intentional edit.
follow_up.closure: Seed malformed text, export exact original bytes before and after an edit, and confirm ordinary backup still contains validated current project data. If recovery-key writes fail, retain download access without pretending durable recovery exists.

follow_up.title: Offer a current backup inside replacement confirmation
follow_up.current_state: Whole-workspace replacement is explicitly confirmed, but the dialog does not provide an in-context current-backup action. This is a usability proposal, not an unauthorized-overwrite finding.
follow_up.action: Add an accessible Download current backup action and inspectable project counts/names if useful. Preserve the current replacement contract; defer automatic merge/undo machinery until demonstrated need.
follow_up.closure: The user can preserve current valid projects before replacement, cancel without changes and restore the exported prior workspace. Legacy GPT data remains isolated.

follow_up.title: Provide an executable manual-use and recipient handoff
follow_up.current_state: Unsupported hosts need a manual fallback, but non-software package README files do not establish a complete run/read-order recipe for the recipient.
follow_up.action: For the first exemplar, give a short read order for root contract and skill files, supported installation layout, input example, manual-use alternative, unavailable-reference handling and result-return instructions. Have a receiver follow it without inherited chat context.
follow_up.closure: The receiver identifies the source revision, necessary constraints and fallback limitations, performs the task, returns observed evidence and removes temporary packaging. Manual mode is not labeled native host support.
follow_up.conditional_dependencies: Draft after selecting the FND-04 source/task, before the recipient run. Manual fallback may precede native host discovery; reuse the exemplar receipt.

follow_up.title: Document tested PowerShell launch commands
follow_up.current_state: Local usage documentation uses POSIX inline environment assignments, which PowerShell cannot execute as written. This release translated those commands manually.
follow_up.action: Add clearly labeled PowerShell environment setup beside POSIX commands or document a tested existing portable launcher. Record OS/shell/runtime/base path and a receiving host acknowledgement in the compact handoff.
follow_up.closure: A clean Windows/PowerShell receiver launches the exact preview/base path and build from the documented commands, verifies export/recovery and acknowledges the exact source and scope.

follow_up.title: Pair source rollback with an older-compatible project backup
follow_up.current_state: The current app reads older v1 backups by supplying new portability defaults. Older builds reject backups containing new fields; source rollback alone is not project-data rollback.
follow_up.action: Immediately preserve available pre-upgrade originals and current exports before recovery/schema edits. Record which originals exist and which are unavailable. Then record a version matrix and exercise current acceptance of old backups plus explicit older-build rejection of new fields without mutation.
follow_up.closure: Rollback can recover the original project using its compatible original backup. New conversion fields remain preserved in the current export; unsupported backward imports fail visibly and never mutate the stored workspace.
follow_up.conditional_dependencies: Immediately preserve and identify any existing pre-upgrade originals before recovery/schema changes; do not invent missing old backups. FND-24â€“25 supply later matrix/transfer evidence before broader rollback claims.
